G1-S1-A: SEO helps your pages rank in search results. AEO (answer engine optimisation) shapes content so it can be lifted into direct answers and featured snippets. GEO (generative engine optimisation) helps AI assistants understand your brand well enough to mention it. They overlap heavily, so most small businesses should plan them as one job.
G1-S3-A: AEO, answer engine optimisation, is about being the answer, not just a link. It means writing pages that open with a clear, direct reply to a real question, structuring them with helpful headings and lists and marking them up so search engines and assistants can pick out the answer confidently.
G1-S4-A: GEO stands for generative engine optimisation. It's the work of making your brand easy for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini to understand, trust and name. It builds on SEO basics, then adds consistent brand facts across the web and content that answers questions in plain, quotable language.
G1-S5-H2: How they overlap, and why you plan them together
G1-S5-A: A small business usually needs all three, but not as three projects. One plan covers them: fix the technical basics, build pages around the questions buyers ask, open each with a direct answer and make your brand facts consistent everywhere. That single body of work serves search rankings, featured answers and AI mentions at the same time.

G1-FAQ-H2: Questions people ask about SEO, AEO and GEO
G1-FAQ-1-Q: Is SEO dead now that people use AI?
G1-FAQ-1-A: No. AI answers still need sources, and Google says the same SEO best practices apply to its AI Overviews and AI Mode, with no special extra optimisation required. Pages that are easy to crawl, clear and genuinely helpful give search engines and AI assistants something worth showing.
G1-FAQ-2-Q: Is GEO the same as geotargeting?
G1-FAQ-2-A: No. In older SEO talk, geo usually meant geotargeting: showing the right pages or ads to people in a particular place. GEO in the AI sense means generative engine optimisation, making your brand easy for AI assistants to understand and mention. Same letters, different jobs. Context usually tells you which.
G1-FAQ-3-Q: How long do SEO, AEO and GEO take to work?
G1-FAQ-3-A: Longer than ads, and nobody can give you an honest fixed date. Technical fixes can land early. Rankings and AI mentions build more slowly, as search engines recrawl your site and learn to trust your content. Because all three rest on the same foundations, progress on one usually helps the others.
G1-FAQ-4-A: No. Nobody controls what AI assistants say, just as nobody controls Google's results. Be wary of anyone selling guaranteed placement. What you can control is how clearly your brand is described on your own site and elsewhere. You can also control how directly your pages answer the questions people actually ask.
G1-FAQ-5-A: Probably not yet. llms.txt is an optional file some sites add to point AI tools at their key pages. It's cheap to add, but it isn't a confirmed ranking signal. Google says you don't need AI text files to appear in its AI features. Get the basics right first.
